stem: Which of the following is most likely to cause a homonymous hemianopia:
fact: A posterior cerebral artery stroke affecting the occipital visual cortex can cause a contralateral homonymous hemianopia, often with macular sparing.
mnemonic: PCA = Posterior Cortical Area: think contralateral field loss.
finding: The review localizes homonymous hemianopia with macular sparing to the contralateral occipital lobe, supplied predominantly by the posterior cerebral artery.

stem: The right and left cerebral hemispheres are partially separated by which of the following structures:
fact: The median longitudinal fissure separates the right and left cerebral hemispheres; the falx cerebri occupies the fissure.
mnemonic: Longitudinal = runs between the two long cerebral halves.
finding: The deep longitudinal fissure separates the cerebral hemispheres, which remain connected by the corpus callosum.

stem: What type of visual field defect are you most likely to see in a lesion of the optic tract:
fact: Each optic tract carries information from the contralateral visual field of both eyes, so an optic-tract lesion causes contralateral homonymous hemianopia.
mnemonic: Tract takes the opposite track: optic tract = opposite homonymous loss.
finding: The review’s localization table maps homonymous hemianopia to a contralateral optic-tract lesion.

stem: Which of the following spinal tracts conveys nociceptive input from the contralateral side of the body:
fact: The lateral spinothalamic tract carries pain and temperature information after the pathway crosses to the contralateral side of the spinal cord.
mnemonic: Lateral STT = Lateral Sensation of Temperature and pain.
finding: The lateral spinothalamic pathway carries pain and temperature; these pathways cross and ascend contralaterally.

stem: Which of the following best describes the function of the foramen of Monro:
options: Major site of production of CSF
Connects the lateral ventricles to the third ventricle
Drains CSF into the subarachnoid cisterns
Connects the third ventricle to the fourth ventricle
Connects the right and left lateral ventricles
fact: The interventricular foramina of Monro connect each lateral ventricle with the third ventricle and allow CSF to pass between them.
mnemonic: Monro means ‘moves’ CSF from lateral ventricles to the midline third ventricle.
finding: The ventricular-system reference states that each lateral ventricle communicates with the third ventricle through the interventricular foramen of Monro.

stem: A 71 year old man walks into ED following a fall. He is complaining of neck pain and weakness affecting his upper limbs only. Which of the following spinal cord lesions is most likely:
fact: Central cord syndrome typically follows cervical hyperextension in an older patient and causes motor weakness that is greater in the upper than the lower limbs, often with bladder dysfunction.
mnemonic: Central cord: hands are hit harder than legs.
sourceLabel: NCBI Bookshelf central cord syndrome review
finding: The reference describes older adults after low-energy cervical hyperextension with disproportionately greater upper-extremity motor deficits.

stem: The thalamus surrounds which of the following structures:
fact: The paired thalami form the upper and lateral walls around the third ventricle.
mnemonic: Third is between the two thalami: thalamus hugs the third ventricle.
finding: The thalamus reference states that the thalamus forms the upper and lateral walls of the third ventricle.

stem: The primary auditory cortex is located in which of the following regions:
fact: The primary auditory cortex is located in the superior temporal gyrus of the temporal lobe.
mnemonic: Temporal = time and tone: hearing belongs to the temporal lobe.
finding: The cerebral-hemisphere reference locates the primary auditory cortex in the superior temporal gyrus.

stem: The primary somatosensory cortex is located in which of the following regions:
fact: The primary somatosensory cortex lies in the postcentral gyrus of the parietal lobe and processes somatic sensation from the contralateral body.
mnemonic: POSTcentral = sensory; it is posterior in the parietal lobe.
finding: The reference locates the primary somatosensory cortex in the postcentral gyrus immediately posterior to the central sulcus, within the parietal lobe.

stem: Which of the following best describes the position of the frontal lobe:
options: Anterior to the central sulcus and superior to the lateral sulcus
Posterior to the central sulcus and superior to the lateral sulcus
Anterior to the central sulcus and inferior to the lateral sulcus
Posterior to the central sulcus and inferior to the lateral sulcus
fact: The frontal lobe lies anterior to the central sulcus and superior to the lateral sulcus (lateral fissure).
mnemonic: Frontal is in front of central and above lateral.
finding: The anatomy chapter states that the frontal lobe lies anterior to the central sulcus and above the lateral sulcus.
